newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy shares end well off highs, bond futures weigh.
newsitem.headline: Italy shares end well off highs, bond futures weigh.

text.p: Italian shares wiped out a large part of the session's gains in desultory late trade, moving lower in the wake of a fall in Btp bond future prices.

Stocks moved up early on but the market showed little reaction as the government expectedly won a confidence vote on the last chunk of the 1997 budget. Wall Street gave no help with the Dow rangebound ahead of Wednesday's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony by Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan.
The all-share Mibtel index closed up 0.38 pct at 12,324 after a session high at 12.390. The Mib30 blue chip index ended up 0.37 pct at 18,379 after a 18,493 peak.
Dealers cited general uncertainty with some expecting a fresh technical correction. "We're in a wait-and-see phase and I think the market has a little bit further to fall," one trader said.
Btp bond futures ended around session lows in a technical market after breaking a series of support levels.

San Paolo bank again outperformed among blue chips on its strong 1996 profit figures and sale of its 40 percent stake in Crediop to Franco-Belgian Dexia. The stock closed 3.07 percent up at 12,205 lire.
Banco Ambrosiano Veneto closed 1.32 percent up at 4,290 after reporting a rise in 1996 parent net.
Fiat, among shares seeing selective interest, put on 1.57 percent to 5,312 lire.
Financial holding Gemina rose 1.09 percent to 979.2 lire after bourse watchdog Consob gave green light for the listing of HPI, grouping Gemina's former industrial interests after its spinoff.
Olivetti gained 1.42 percent to 627.5 lire but energy group ENI lost 1.05 percent to 8,832.
Telecoms holding Stet slipped 0.99 percent to 8,022 after a new board was named today to oversee its privatisation. But Telecom Italia gained 0.46 percent to 4,354 lire.
